sections.title: Reading I: A Tour to Central Zoo (timetable)

Writing: interpreting a timetable and filling in a form

summary: A timetable lists activities and times; for "how long", subtract one time from another (9:15 → 9:45 = 30 minutes).
The zoo notice: tour on 24th June, led by Mrs. Karki; four animal groups — birds, reptiles, mammals, amphibians; attendance twice.
The request letter: thanks → problem (too few computers, little software, no internet) → polite request with would; closes Yours faithfully.
can = present ability/informal request; could = past ability/polite request; would = very polite request, imagined result, wish, would rather.
Modal + base verb; no -s; question = modal first.
Present simple: habits, facts, timetables; he/she/it + -s/-es/-ies; does/doesn't + base verb.
Interpreting a timetable = turning it into connected sentences in order.

summary: Story: the boy travels alone; his father's note says he is in the adjacent compartment, and the boy's fear vanishes — a parent's love protects quietly.
Poem: the speaker failed to change the world, nation, town and family; he learns that change begins with himself and spreads outward.
Yes/no question = helping verb + subject + …; use do/does/did when there is no helping verb, then the base verb.
some becomes any in questions; short answers use the helping verb.
Permission: Can/May I…?, Is it okay if I…?, Would you mind if I + past?; "Not at all" means yes.
ed endings: /t/, /d/, /ɪd/ (/ɪd/ only after t or d).

summary: Announcements give what, when, where, who and end with a request and thanks.
Flight RA-402, Kathmandu → New Delhi: seatbelts, baggage under seat or overhead, seat upright, gadgets off, no smoking.
Parents Day: 22nd March, 11 a.m., Assembly Hall, 42nd anniversary, chief guest the Mayor of Bardaghat (an ex-student).
Reported yes/no question: asked + if/whether + subject + verb, tense one step back, no question mark.
Present reporting verb (says/asks) → no tense change.
Instructions: title, numbered steps, imperative verbs, warnings.
Washing: separate → load → detergent → turn on → cycle → temperature → clean.

Writing I: An account of a memorable event

summary: A memoir and a diary are first-person, true, mostly past-tense records with feelings; a diary has date, Dear Diary, events, feelings, reflection.
Mustang memoir: Pokhara → Tatopani (hot spring, 7 hours) → Kagbeni (Kali Gandaki) → Muktinath (Hindu and Buddhist; five-colour flags) → Marpha (apples, flat roofs, alleyways).
Neil's diary: Dhading village with a Nepali friend; bumpy bus, songs, family lunch; admires Nepali friendliness.
Present perfect = has/have + pp, linked to now (ever, never, yet, since, for). Past simple = finished time (yesterday, ago, last…).
since + point of time; for + length of time.

sections.title: Reading I: The Old Woman and the Lime Tree

summary: Folk tale: six wishes — cart, hut, livestock, money, power, the village's labour; the last wish loses everything. Moral: greed brings ruin.
Poem Free Birds: students = free birds (metaphor); overcome hindrances with determination; value time; be patriots.
Reported imperatives: reporting verb + person + (not) to + base verb.
Choose the verb by purpose: told/ordered, asked/requested, advised, warned/forbade.
say takes no person object; tell does.
Skeleton story: past tense, every clue, title, moral.

units.title: Traditional Wedding Customs around the World / Life Saving Inventions

sections.title: Reading I: Traditional Wedding Customs around the World

summary: Weddings: India (engagement, Mehendi, garlands), Japan (costume changes, san-san-kudo with sake, money in envelopes), Jamaica (whole village, review of the bride, black cake), Wales (wooden spoon, "kidnapped" bride).
Inventions: Hippo-roller (90 L), LifeStraw (cleans up to 1,000 L), AidPod (medicine in Coca-Cola crates, tested in Zambia).
Causatives: have/make/let + person + base verb; get + person + to + verb; have/get + thing + past participle; passive be made to.
Agreement: and → plural; either/or → nearer subject; with/including do not change the subject; gerunds and sums → singular.
Paraphrase = same meaning, new words and structures, nothing added.

summary: Weather table: Nepalgunj hottest (36.6 °C); Pokhara most rain (40.2 mm); Nepalgunj, Ghorahi, Janakpur no rain; Kathmandu coolest.
Migration = moving to live elsewhere; push factors drive out, pull factors attract.
Benefits: labour, business, skills, culture; drawbacks: brain drain, low pay, environmental pressure, cultural displacement.
will: decision now, opinion prediction, offer, condition.
be going to: plan, prediction from evidence.
will have + pp (+ by…): finished before a future time.

sections.title: Grammar I: Past simple, past continuous, past perfect

summary: Having Fun: the son planned mischief; the father put coins in the shoes; the farmer could buy medicine and food. Lesson: real joy is in giving.

Inventions in the text: Watt (steam engine), Stephenson (locomotive), Daimler (car, 1885), Faraday (electricity), Wright brothers (aeroplane, 1903), Sputnik 1 (1957), Marconi (radio), Baird (TV), Bell (telephone, 1876), Fessenden (wireless telephone, 1900), Cooper (mobile phone).
Past continuous = background action; past simple = interrupting action; past perfect = earlier action.
used to / didn't use to / did … use to for past habits.
Narrative essay: what, when, where, what happened, feelings.

Smartphones: one device for everything; easy information makes us lazier; constant connection is tiring; they replaced landlines, desktops and cameras.
Comparatives: -er / more; superlatives: the -est / the most; irregular good–better–best, bad–worse–worst.
than; as … as; not as … as; never more better.
Adverbs: hard–harder, carefully–more carefully, well–better–best.
Comparison writing: point by point, with whereas, while, both, unlike.

at times, on days/dates, in months/years/parts of the day; on time / in time.
Question tags: opposite polarity, same auxiliary, pronoun; aren't I, shall we, positive tag after never/hardly/nobody.

Khaptad NP: est. 1984, 225 km², four districts of Sudurpaschim, 22 patans, Khaptad Daha, Triveni, Sahashra Linga (3,276 m), 266 birds, 23 mammals; entry Rs. 100 for Nepalis.
who people, which things, whose possession, where place, when time; that not after a comma.
a/an by sound; the for specific/unique/superlative/instruments; no article for meals, sports, languages.

Nepal has more than 880 bird species.
Poem: the teacher eats the homework — because it is a cooking class; rhyme in lines 2 and 4; surprise ending.
enjoy/mind/avoid/finish/keep + -ing; want/would like/agree/learn/decide + to; preposition + -ing.
Wh-question = wh + auxiliary + subject + verb; subject questions need no do.

Countable: many, a few, fewer; uncountable: much, a little, less; both: some, any, a lot of, enough, no.
some in positives and offers; any in negatives and questions.
Describing a chart: introduction, overview, details with numbers, trend words.
Process description: passive + first, then, next, finally.

Poem: second-conditional wishes — fly, jump towers, clean the oceans, save nature, feed the poor, make the world better.
Zero: if + present, present. Type 1: if + present, will. Type 2: if + past, would. Type 3: if + had + V3, would have + V3.
No will/would in the if-clause; If I were… in formal English.
News story: headline, byline, dateline, lead (5W1H), body.

summary: Natural habitat = where a creature and its ancestors have always lived; wild creatures cannot survive long elsewhere.
Conservation moved from banning hunting/poaching/overfishing to saving whole habitats; threats: deforestation, global warming; extinction is permanent.
The biosphere gives food, building materials, fuel, medicine; destroying it threatens humans.
Notice (26 Poush 2078): schools closed 27 Poush–15 Magh due to COVID-19; vaccination for 12–17-year-olds.
because + clause / because of + noun; so that + clause / (in order) to + verb; although + clause / in spite of + noun or -ing; however starts a new sentence.
Opinion essay: opinion → reasons with examples → other side → conclusion.

is being, was being, has been, had been, will be, will have been, must be + V3.

too + adj + to (negative result); adj + enough + to (positive result); too young = not old enough.
Agreement: and → plural; everyone / one of / amounts / -ics → singular; or → nearer subject; some of + plural → plural.

now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there, this → that.
